title: Pato tim
intro: A whole duck braised slowly with soy sauce, star anise, ginger and dried shiitake until the meat is tender enough to pull apart with chopsticks. It is served on a bed of bok choy under its dark, glossy sauce, usually for a special family meal.

items.name: water
items.note: about, to come halfway up the duck

steps.text: Soak the shiitake in the hot water until soft. Squeeze them out, cut off the stems and strain the soaking liquid to keep it.
Pat the duck dry and trim the excess fat around the cavity. Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium heat and brown the duck on all sides, turning it carefully.
Lift out the duck and pour off all but 2 tablespoons of the fat. Sauté the ginger, garlic and green onions until fragrant.

Return the duck breast side up. Add the soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, star anise, wine, mushrooms, their soaking liquid and enough water to come halfway up the duck. Bring to a boil.
Cover, lower the heat and simmer, turning the duck and spooning the sauce over it every 30 minutes, until the leg meat is very tender and pulls away from the bone.
Gently lift the duck onto a platter. Skim the fat off the sauce and boil it until reduced to about 2 cups.
Meanwhile, blanch the bok choy in boiling salted water, drain and arrange it around the duck.
Stir the cornstarch mixture into the sauce and cook until glossy. Taste for salt, then pour the sauce and mushrooms over the duck and serve with rice.

tips: Pato tim tastes even better the next day: chill the sauce, lift off the hardened fat and reheat the duck in it. Save the skimmed duck fat for frying rice or potatoes.

title: Pinaupong manok
intro: A whole chicken stuffed with lemongrass, onion, garlic and tomato, then cooked sitting on a bed of rock salt and banana leaves in a covered pot. The salt roasts it gently, so the meat comes out juicy and aromatic with lightly golden skin.

steps.text: Pat the chicken dry and rub it inside and out with the fish sauce, salt and pepper.
Stuff the cavity with the lemongrass, onion, garlic and tomatoes and tie the legs together.
Spread the rock salt evenly over the bottom of a heavy, deep pot (cast iron or thick aluminum, not nonstick), about 2 cm thick. Lay the banana leaves over the salt.
Set the chicken breast side up on the leaves and cover the pot tightly.
Cook over medium heat until you hear the salt crackling.
Lower the heat to low and cook, covered and without lifting the lid, until the thigh reads 165°F (74°C) and the juices run clear.
Rest the chicken for 10 minutes, then carve. Mix the soy sauce and calamansi juice for the dip and serve with rice and the juices from the cavity.

tips: Open a window: the bottom leaves char and smell smoky, which is part of the flavor. Discard the salt afterward, and let the pot cool completely before washing.

title: Ginisang atay ng manok
intro: Chicken livers quickly sautéed with garlic, onion, tomato and bell pepper in a little soy and oyster sauce. Creamy inside and savory, it is a cheap, fast ulam that needs only rice.

items.name: chicken livers
items.note: trimmed of sinew and any green spots, halved

steps.text: Rinse the livers, drain well and pat dry.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over high heat. Sear the livers in a single layer until browned on one side, turn and brown briefly. They should still be pink inside. Scoop them out.
Lower the heat to medium and sauté the garlic, onion and tomatoes until the tomatoes soften.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce, water and pepper and simmer.
Return the livers with the bell pepper and simmer until the livers are just cooked through, with only a trace of pink.
Stir in the green onions and serve with rice.

tips: Overcooked liver turns grainy and bitter, so take it off the heat as soon as it is done. A few cubes of fried potato make the dish go further.

title: Chicken liver steak
intro: Chicken livers seared and tossed in a bistek-style sauce of soy sauce and calamansi, topped with soft onion rings. Rich, salty and tangy, it is a quick, budget-friendly dish for rice.

steps.text: Pat the livers dry, toss with 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce and the pepper, then dust with the cornstarch.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Fry the onion rings until just soft and set aside.
Add the remaining oil and sear the livers in batches, 1 to 2 minutes per side, until browned outside and slightly pink inside. Set aside.
Lower the heat, add the garlic and stir until fragrant, then add the remaining soy sauce, the calamansi juice, water and sugar. Simmer until slightly reduced.
Return the livers and onion rings and toss in the sauce until the livers are just cooked through.
Serve right away with rice.

tips: Buy livers that are glossy and deep red-brown. Cook them just until the pink fades in the center; any longer and they turn dry and bitter.

title: Ginisang balunbalunan
intro: Chicken gizzards simmered until tender, then sliced and sautéed with garlic, onion and bell pepper in a savory soy and oyster sauce. Pleasantly chewy and full of flavor, it is a frugal ulam that also works as pulutan.

steps.text: Rinse the gizzards and put them in a pot with the ginger, bay leaves, peppercorns, salt and water. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Cover and simmer until the gizzards are tender when pierced with a fork.
Drain, keeping 1/4 cup of the broth. Slice the gizzards about 1 cm thick.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and fry the gizzards until the edges brown lightly.
Add the garlic and onion and cook until soft.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce, reserved broth and pepper and toss until glossy.
Add the bell peppers and chili and cook until just tender. Serve with rice.

tips: A pressure cooker gets the gizzards tender in about 15 minutes. Boiled gizzards keep for 3 days in the fridge, ready for a quick stir-fry.

title: Sweet and sour chicken
intro: Crisp fried chicken bites tossed in a bright sweet and sour sauce with pineapple, bell peppers, onion and carrot. Tangy, glossy and a little sweet, it is a favorite with kids and at family lunches.

steps.text: Season the chicken with salt and pepper, toss with the beaten egg, then coat well in the cornstarch.
Heat the frying oil to 350°F (175°C) and fry the chicken in two batches, about 6 minutes each, until golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack.
For the sauce, heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok and sauté the garlic, onion and carrot for a couple of minutes.
Add the pineapple juice, vinegar, banana ketchup, sugar and soy sauce. Let it boil for a minute without stirring, then stir.
Add the bell peppers and pineapple chunks and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture and cook until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Toss the fried chicken in the sauce just before serving, with rice.

tips: Toss the chicken in the sauce at the last minute so it stays crisp, or serve the sauce on the side. Pork cubes or fish fillet work the same way.

title: Chicken and broccoli in oyster sauce
intro: Tender slices of chicken stir-fried with broccoli and carrots in a glossy garlic and oyster sauce. Ready in about half an hour, it is an everyday ulam that gets vegetables onto the table.

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the soy sauce and cornstarch and let it sit.
Blanch the broccoli and carrot in boiling salted water, then drain well.
Stir the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, water and cornstarch together for the sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the chicken until cooked through. Scoop it out.
Stir-fry the garlic, ginger and onion until fragrant.
Return the chicken, add the vegetables, then stir the sauce and pour it in. Toss until the sauce thickens and coats everything. Serve with rice.

tips: Blanching keeps the broccoli bright green and lets the stir-fry stay fast. Mushrooms or snow peas are good additions.

title: Chicken fingers
intro: Strips of chicken breast seasoned with calamansi and garlic, breaded in crunchy panko and fried golden. Served with a mayo-ketchup dip, they are a lunchbox and party favorite with kids.

items.name: boneless chicken breast
items.note: cut into finger-length strips about 1.5 cm thick

steps.text: Toss the chicken strips with the calamansi juice, salt, garlic powder and pepper.
Set out three shallow bowls: flour, beaten eggs and panko.
Coat each strip in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing so the crumbs stick. Lay on a tray.
Heat oil about 2 cm deep in a pan to 350°F (175°C). Fry the strips in batches, turning once, about 4 minutes per batch, until golden and cooked through.
Drain on a rack. Mix the mayonnaise and banana ketchup for the dip and serve with rice.

tips: Breaded strips freeze well: freeze them on a tray, bag them once firm and fry straight from frozen, adding about 2 minutes.

title: Chicken katsu
intro: Chicken thighs pounded thin, coated in panko and fried into crisp golden cutlets, then sliced and served with a sweet-savory katsu sauce and shredded cabbage. It is a popular home and canteen lunch with rice.

steps.text: Pound the chicken between two sheets of plastic to an even 1 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Dredge each piece in flour, dip in egg, then press firmly into the panko to coat.
Heat oil about 1.5 cm deep in a wide pan to 340°F (170°C). Fry two cutlets at a time, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on a rack and rest for 2 minutes, then slice into strips.
Stir the ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce and sugar together until the sugar dissolves.
Serve the katsu with the cabbage, sauce and rice.

tips: Rest the fried cutlets on a rack, not on paper, so the underside stays crisp. Leftover katsu reheats well in an oven toaster.

title: Homemade chicken nuggets
intro: Ground chicken mixed with grated carrot and onion, shaped into nuggets, breaded and fried until golden. They are softer and juicier than the frozen kind and easy to make ahead for baon.

steps.text: Mix the ground chicken, carrot, onion, egg, bread crumbs, salt, garlic powder and pepper. Fry a small piece to taste for salt. Cover and chill to firm up.
With wet hands, shape tablespoons of the mixture into about 30 nuggets, flattening each to about 1 cm thick.
Coat each nugget in flour, then egg, then bread crumbs.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C) and fry the nuggets in batches, about 4 minutes per batch, turning once, until golden and cooked through.
Drain on a rack and serve with banana ketchup and rice.

tips: Freeze breaded, uncooked nuggets on a tray, then bag them. Fry from frozen at slightly lower heat, about 6 minutes, so the centers cook through.

title: Honey garlic chicken
intro: Chicken wings fried until crisp, then tossed in a sticky glaze of honey, soy sauce, garlic and calamansi. Sweet, salty and garlicky, they disappear fast at the table.

steps.text: Pat the wings dry, season with salt and pepper and toss in the cornstarch, shaking off the excess.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C) and fry the wings in two batches, about 12 minutes per batch, until golden, crisp and cooked through. Drain on a rack.
For the glaze, melt the butter in a wide pan over medium-low heat and cook the garlic until fragrant and pale golden.
Add the honey, soy sauce, calamansi juice and water and simmer until syrupy, with big, slow bubbles.
Add the wings and toss until coated and shiny. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve with rice.

tips: Honey burns quickly, so keep the heat at medium-low once it goes in. The same glaze works on pan-fried boneless thighs.

title: Salted egg chicken
intro: Crisp fried chicken bites coated in a rich, sandy sauce of salted egg yolks cooked in butter with garlic and chili. Salty, buttery and a little sweet, it is very rich, so a little goes a long way with rice.

steps.text: Season the chicken with salt and pepper, toss with the beaten egg, then coat in the cornstarch.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C) and fry the chicken in two batches, about 6 minutes each, until golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack.
Mash the salted egg yolks with a fork until fine and crumbly.
Melt the butter in a wok over low heat and cook the garlic and chili until fragrant.
Add the yolks and stir constantly until they foam and smell rich and toasty.
Stir in the evaporated milk and sugar and cook until the sauce is thick and creamy.
Take the wok off the heat, add the chicken and toss until every piece is coated. Serve right away.

tips: Keep the heat low for the sauce; salted egg yolk scorches fast. Chop the leftover salted egg whites with tomato and onion for a quick side dish.

title: Chicken pastil
intro: Shredded chicken cooked down with garlic, onion, ginger and soy sauce until dry, savory and lightly crisp, then spooned over rice and wrapped in banana leaves. Pastil is filling and portable, and the chicken flakes keep well for several days.

items.name: banana leaves
items.note: about 25 cm squares, wilted over a flame

steps.text: Put the chicken in a pot with the water and salt, bring to a boil and skim. Simmer, covered, until cooked through.
Lift out the chicken and let it cool enough to handle, keeping 1/2 cup of the broth. Discard the skin and bones and shred the meat very finely with forks or your fingers.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the garlic, onion and ginger until soft and lightly golden.
Add the shredded chicken, soy sauce, sugar, pepper and reserved broth. Cook, stirring often, until the liquid is gone.
Lower the heat and keep stirring and pressing the chicken against the pan until it is dry, fluffy and browned in spots.
Stir in the chilies and taste for salt.
To wrap, put a cup of rice in the middle of each banana leaf and flatten it slightly. Top with 2 to 3 tablespoons of chicken flakes and fold the leaf over into a neat packet. Serve warm.

tips: Kept in a covered jar in the fridge, the chicken flakes last about a week. Rewarm them in a dry pan before wrapping fresh rice.

title: Chicken satti
intro: Small chicken skewers grilled and served swimming in a red, spicy, slightly sweet sauce flavored with annatto, chili, curry and peanut. It is eaten with puso or plain rice, at breakfast or any meal.

steps.text: Mix the chicken with the soy sauce, sugar, garlic, curry powder and pepper. Cover and refrigerate while the skewers soak.
Thread 4 or 5 pieces of chicken onto each skewer.
For the sauce, warm the oil with the annatto powder in a saucepan over low heat until it turns red. Add the onion, garlic and ginger and cook until soft.
Stir in the chili flakes and curry powder for 30 seconds, then add the broth, peanut butter, sugar, soy sauce and vinegar. Simmer, stirring, until slightly thickened.
Grill the skewers over medium-hot coals or on a grill pan, turning often, until cooked through and charred in spots.
Lay the skewers in bowls, ladle the hot sauce over and serve with puso or rice.

tips: The sauce should be thin enough to soak into the rice. Thin it with a little broth if it gets too thick on standing.

title: Lemon chicken
intro: Thin chicken fillets fried in a crisp cornstarch coating and served under a glossy, sweet-tart lemon sauce. Bright and tangy, it is a lauriat-style dish that is easy to make at home.

steps.text: Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Dip each fillet in egg, then coat in the mixed cornstarch and flour.
Heat oil about 1 cm deep in a wide pan to 340°F (170°C). Fry the fillets in batches, about 3 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack.
For the sauce, simmer the lemon juice, zest, sugar, water and salt in a small saucepan until the sugar dissolves.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture and cook until the sauce is clear and glossy, then stir in the butter.
Slice the chicken, lay it on a platter and pour the hot sauce over just before serving.

tips: Calamansi juice works in place of lemon; taste and add a little more sugar if it is too sharp. Pour the sauce at the table so the coating stays crisp.

title: Chicken cordon bleu
intro: Chicken breasts rolled around ham and cheese, breaded and fried until golden, then sliced to show the melted center and served with a creamy cheese sauce. It is a special-occasion dish that is easier than it looks.

items.name: large boneless chicken breasts
items.note: about 600 g, each halved horizontally into 2 thin cutlets

steps.text: Pound each cutlet between sheets of plastic to about 0.5 cm thick and season with salt and pepper.
Lay a slice of ham and a stick of cheese at one end of each cutlet. Roll up tightly, tucking in the sides so the cheese is sealed in, and secure with toothpicks.
Coat each roll in flour, then egg, then bread crumbs. Chill so the coating sets.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 325°F (160°C). Fry two rolls at a time, turning, about 12 minutes per batch, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on a rack and rest for 5 minutes, then remove the toothpicks and slice.

For the sauce, melt the butter in a small pan, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk. Simmer, whisking, until thick, then stir in the cheese until melted. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve the sliced rolls with the cheese sauce and rice.

tips: To bake instead, set the breaded rolls on a greased rack and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 30 to 35 minutes, turning once. Seal the ends well or the cheese leaks out.

title: Cashew chicken
intro: Diced chicken stir-fried with crunchy toasted cashews, bell peppers, carrots and onion in a savory oyster sauce. Quick and colorful, it is a lauriat favorite that suits a weeknight.

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the soy sauce and cornstarch and let it sit. Stir the sauce ingredients together in a cup.
Toast the cashews in a dry wok over medium-low heat, stirring, until golden. Tip them out.
Heat the oil in the wok over high heat and stir-fry the chicken until browned and cooked through. Scoop it out.
Stir-fry the garlic, ginger, onion and carrot until the onion softens.
Add the bell peppers and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return the chicken, stir the sauce and pour it in. Toss until thick and glossy, then stir in the cashews and serve with rice.

tips: Add the cashews at the very end so they stay crunchy. Roasted salted cashews work too; cut back a little on the soy sauce.

title: Chicken giniling
intro: Ground chicken sautéed with tomato sauce, diced potatoes, carrots, green peas and raisins into a saucy, slightly sweet mince. It is a quick, kid-friendly ulam that also makes a good filling for omelets and pandesal.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and fry the potato and carrot until the edges turn golden. Scoop them out.
In the same pan, sauté the garlic and onion until soft.
Add the ground chicken and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until no longer pink.
Stir in the fish sauce, then the tomato sauce and water. Return the potato and carrot, cover and simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Add the peas, raisins and bell pepper and simmer uncovered until the sauce thickens slightly.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with rice.

tips: Leftovers make a quick torta: beat 3 eggs, stir in a cup of giniling and fry in patties until set.

title: Chicken binagoongan
intro: Chicken simmered in sautéed shrimp paste with garlic, onion, tomato and a splash of vinegar, with soft slices of eggplant to soak up the sauce. Salty, savory and deeply flavored, it needs plenty of rice.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken on both sides. Scoop it out.
Sauté the garlic, onion and tomatoes until the tomatoes break down.
Stir in the shrimp paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the water and bring to a boil. Pour in the vinegar and let it boil without stirring.
Cover and simmer until the chicken is tender.
Add the eggplant and chilies and simmer, uncovered, until the eggplant is soft and the sauce has thickened.
Stir in the sugar, taste and adjust, then serve with rice.

tips: Shrimp paste brands differ in saltiness: start with less, taste after the simmer and add more if needed. Fry the eggplant slices first if you want them to hold their shape.

title: Chicken humba
intro: Chicken braised in soy sauce, vinegar and brown sugar with salted black beans and dried lily buds until the sauce is dark, sweet and sticky. It is sweeter and richer than adobo, and the sauce is the best part over rice.

steps.text: Soak the lily buds in warm water until soft. Drain, trim the hard ends and tie each bud in a knot.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken on both sides.
Add the garlic and onion and cook until fragrant.
Add the soy sauce, water, bay leaves, peppercorns and star anise and bring to a boil. Pour in the vinegar and boil without stirring.
Cover, lower the heat and simmer until the chicken is tender.
Add the tausi, lily buds and brown sugar and simmer uncovered, turning the chicken now and then, until the sauce is thick and sticky.
Remove the bay leaves and star anise and serve with rice.

tips: Some cooks add a splash of pineapple juice with the soy sauce for a fruitier sauce. Like adobo, humba tastes even better the next day.

title: Chicken kare-kare
intro: Chicken and vegetables in a thick, nutty peanut sauce colored with annatto and thickened with toasted ground rice. The sauce is mild on its own, so every bite gets a dab of sautéed shrimp paste on the side.

items.name: banana blossom
items.note: outer leaves removed, sliced and soaked in salted water

steps.text: Toast the uncooked rice in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until deep golden. Let it cool, then grind it fine in a blender or spice grinder.
Put the chicken, water, quartered onion and salt in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim and simmer, covered, until tender.

Lift out the chicken and keep 3 cups of the broth. Cook the vegetables one kind at a time in the rest of the boiling broth until just tender: banana blossom about 5 minutes, string beans and eggplant about 3 minutes each, bok choy 1 minute. Drain.
In another pot, warm the oil with the annatto powder until red, then sauté the chopped onion and garlic until soft.
Add the chicken, the 3 cups of broth and the peanut butter. Stir until the peanut butter dissolves, then simmer.
Sprinkle in the ground rice, stirring, and simmer until the sauce is thick enough to coat a spoon. Season with the fish sauce and salt.
Arrange the vegetables over or beside the chicken and serve with rice and shrimp paste.

tips: If you use sweetened peanut butter, skip any sugar and lean on the shrimp paste for balance. Natural peanut butter gives a deeper, nuttier sauce.

title: Garlic butter chicken
intro: Bone-in chicken thighs pan-seared until the skin is crisp, then bathed in sizzling garlic butter brightened with calamansi and a touch of soy sauce. Savory and rich, it is great with garlic rice or plain rice.

steps.text: Pat the chicken very dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Lay the thighs skin side down and cook without moving them until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Turn the thighs, cover and cook over medium-low heat until cooked through, 165°F (74°C) at the bone.
Move the chicken to a plate. Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of fat, add the butter and garlic and cook until the garlic is pale golden.
Add the calamansi juice, soy sauce and broth and simmer, scraping up the browned bits, until slightly reduced.
Return the chicken skin side up and spoon the garlic butter over it. Warm for 1 minute, scatter the green onions and serve.

tips: Keep the sauce off the skin until serving so it stays crisp. Leftover garlic butter from the pan is excellent stirred into rice.
